hero.title: Test: Am I in love with my BFF?
hero.description: Feelings for your best friend can grow over time, and that's normal. Seeing each other all the time, laughing, having a good time together: it's only human. With this test, try to see your feelings more clearly, and find out what you truly feel!
hero.subtitle: Free, no sign-up, nobody sees your answers

section1.title: In love with your best friend: why it takes so long to see it
section1.intro: Everyone knows someone it happened to. And most of the time, that person was the last one to notice.
section1.p1: Being in love with your best friend is the most ordinary situation there is, and the hardest one to read. With someone you have just met, the signs are obvious: the knot in your stomach, the phone you check every two minutes. With a friend of ten years, none of that. The signs settled in one by one, without ever making a sound.
section1.p2: So it takes months before you even ask yourself the question. And when it comes, it often comes from outside: someone tells you the two of you would make a good couple, or your friend starts dating someone and you find out it hurts far more than expected.
section1.p3: That is exactly what this test is for: putting words on what you feel, before life forces you to. It relies on what only exists in love, not on what friendship and love have in common. Because enjoying each other's company, trust, laughing until it hurts, all of that exists between friends too, and a test that counted them would tell you that you are in love with half your contacts.
section1.quote: "You don't fall in love with your best friend. One day you realise you already were."

section2.title: Friendship or love: what changes, situation by situation
section2.intro: The same scene, seen by a friend and by someone who is falling in love. Look at which side you recognise yourself on most often.
section2.row1Score: They tell you about a date
section2.row1Level: You want every detail, you give advice
section2.row1Analysis: You change the subject, or find flaws in the person
section2.row2Analysis: You notice it, and you don't want it to end
section2.row3Score: Someone says you would make a good couple
section2.row3Level: You both laugh, and it's forgotten
section2.row3Analysis: You laugh too, and you think about it that night
section2.row4Score: You picture ten years from now
section2.row4Level: You're friends, each with your own life
section2.row4Analysis: You're together, and the picture doesn't shock you

section3.title: The signs that don't lie
section3.p1: Not all signs are equal. Loving to spend time together proves nothing: that is the very definition of a best friend. The signs that count are the ones that have no friendly version.
section3.sub1P1: Not necessarily wanting to sleep together, even if that is the clearest sign. Simply wanting contact: reaching for their hand, letting a hug last, noticing how they smell. Between friends, physical contact is pleasant and forgotten right away. Here, you don't forget it.
section3.sub2P1: A friend is happy when their friend meets someone. If it stings you instead, if you find flaws in everyone they like, if you change the subject when they bring it up, that is not friendship talking.
section3.sub3P1: You meet someone nice, and without meaning to, you compare. And the other person loses. Often. When your dates end with "it's just not the same", it's worth asking: the same as what?
section3.sub4P1: That little question that crosses your mind while watching them laugh. Once, it happens to everyone. If it keeps coming back, if you catch yourself answering it in detail, you are no longer asking a question, you are hoping.

section4.title: How this test works
section4.p1: Fifteen questions, four answers each. You start by saying whether your best friend is a guy or a girl, so the questions talk about the right person, without a "he or she" on every line.
section4.p2: Each answer earns its own number of points, and the questions don't all weigh the same. Having already imagined making love with this person, or picturing yourself living with them as a couple, earns up to twelve points: those wishes don't exist in friendship. Them having met your parents earns four at most, because a best friend meeting the parents is perfectly normal.
section4.p3: Some strong answers guarantee a level: if you have been waiting for that kiss for a long time, the test won't tell you "it's friendship" because of ten lukewarm answers elsewhere. The score runs from 0 to 129, over four levels.
section4.tip: Answer about what you live, not what you would like to live, nor what you would find reasonable. The test judges nothing, and nobody sees your answers.

section5.title: If the result says yes: tell them, or not?
section5.intro: That is the question everyone asks right after. There is no right answer that works for everyone, but there is a method.
section5.pillar1Text: Not the friendship, contrary to what people think: a solid friendship survives a "I thought so too, but no". What you risk is a few awkward weeks. What you risk by saying nothing is years of asking yourself the question.
section5.pillar2Title: Read their signals before you speak
section5.pillar2Text: Do they look for you in a room, touch you more than others, tell you about their dates with a bit too much insistence? There is a test made for exactly that, which looks at whether your friend secretly loves you.
section5.pillar3Text: No grand declaration, no letter. One sentence, in person, in a quiet moment: "I need to tell you something, and you have every right not to feel the same." The rest is for them to say.
section5.pillar4Title: Accept the answer, whatever it is
section5.pillar4Text: A no is not the end of the friendship, on one condition: that you take it as a no, and not as a "not yet". Leave some air, a few weeks, then pick up where you left off. Most friendships survive it very well.

section6.title: If the result says no: keep your friend, with no ulterior motive
section6.p1: A low result is nothing to be disappointed about. What you have with this person, a friendship where you tell each other everything, where you rush to share your good news, is rare, and it is worth no less than a love story.
section6.p2: If the question came to you because someone said you would make a good couple, you can put it away. Other people often project onto two close friends what they would like to see. And if it came because you have been single for a while and this person is the closest one to you, that is normal too: it isn't love, it's missing someone, and your best friend is not the cure for that.
section6.tip: If what you feel looks more like a brand-new attraction to someone you barely know, you need a different test. This one is made for people you know by heart.

seo.faq1Q: Can you be in love with your best friend without realising it?
seo.faq1A: Yes, and it is even the most common case. Everyday closeness installs the signs one by one, so slowly that none of them sets off an alarm. You often realise it through a shock: the friend who starts dating someone, or somebody asking the question out loud.
seo.faq2Q: How do you tell the difference between loving your friend and being in love?
seo.faq2A: Loving a friend means caring about them and wanting their good. Being in love adds three things that have no friendly version: physical desire, jealousy when they meet someone, and picturing a life together. The test only counts those signs.
seo.faq3A: If the result is high and the question is eating at you, yes, most of the time. A solid friendship survives an honest conversation. What damages it is pretending for months. Read their signals first, pick a quiet moment, and say it simply.
seo.faq4Q: What if it's my friend who is in love with me?
seo.faq4A: The signs are the same, the other way round: they look for you in a room, touch you more than others, react badly when you talk about your dates, find flaws in everyone. If you recognise all of that, the conversation will probably be easier than you think.
seo.faq5Q: Does the test work if my best friend is the same sex as me?
seo.faq5A: Yes. The test only asks whether your friend is a guy or a girl, to write the questions with the right pronoun. It asks nothing about you.
seo.faq6Q: Can a friendship turn into a love story?
seo.faq6A: Yes, and plenty of couples started that way. The advantage is that you already know each other, flaws included: no phase where you play a part. The downside is that you have to accept losing the safety of the word "friend". Those who take the step almost all say the same thing: they should have done it sooner.
